name: Editorial collage
purpose: Give an abstract question a subject viewers can recognize.
inputs: A person or object, a key concept, a question, and a point of focus
examples: Psychology: noticing and understanding; history: a person in their time; society: an individual in a group
motion: Establish the subject, introduce the concept, then reveal the question.

text_slots.question: You may not see the whole story

name: Concept comparison
purpose: Put two easily confused ideas on the same visual footing.
inputs: Two concepts, a shared object, and a short explanation for each
examples: Knowing / understanding; intention / outcome; a rule / its application
motion: Establish both sides, then shift emphasis without using a red X to declare a winner.

text_slots.q: One subject. Two ways of understanding.

name: Chapter bookmarks
purpose: Give viewers a route through a longer explanation.
inputs: Two to five short headings, footage, and an active chapter
examples: Observe / question / explain / reconsider; origin / route / connection / impact
motion: Reveal the tall bookmarks in order and use light and position to identify the current chapter.

text_slots.note: Each step makes the question clearer.

name: Evidence collage
purpose: Place a claim beside the evidence and context needed to assess it.
inputs: A source image, a detail to examine, and two levels of explanation
examples: A page and its interpretation; an archive and a person; an image and its context
motion: Bring in the image, open the evidence sheet, and move attention from material to interpretation.

name: People and relationships
purpose: Show who influences whom and through what connection.
inputs: People or entities, a named relationship, and direction
examples: Friends and choices; cities and trade; organizations and rules
motion: Introduce the subjects before drawing their connections.

name: Feedback loop
purpose: Show how a behavior can reinforce itself.
inputs: Three stages, an actual return path, and a possible way out
examples: Expectation / action / feedback; pressure / avoidance / a harder start
motion: Draw one connection at a time and hold the completed loop rather than spinning it.

text_slots.note: Relief can make avoidance more likely next time.

name: Counts and probability
purpose: Place a noticeable result back inside the full sample.
inputs: Total, selected count, unit, and whether the data is illustrative
examples: Three successes in ten attempts; proportions across groups
motion: Show the full set before the subset. The visible objects must match the numbers.

name: Timeline and turning points
purpose: Show how the same subject changes over time.
inputs: Three stages, a subject, a turning point, and verified dates or stage names
examples: Before and after an event; a changing belief; the development of an institution
motion: Keep time moving in one direction and leave enough time to read the turning point.

name: Map focus
purpose: Establish where the story takes place.
inputs: A geographic base, extent, coordinates, place name, and period
examples: Cities, passes, ports, and cultural regions
motion: Move from region to place using one coordinate system for the camera and labels.

text_slots.t: Put the story on the map
text_slots.note: Establish the place before the people and events

name: Routes and connections
inputs: A base map, route coordinates, nodes, sequence, and factual or illustrative status
examples: Migration, trade, diplomatic travel, and the spread of ideas
motion: Grow the route in segments and label each arrival. Animation time is not travel time.

text_slots.t: Follow the route. Find the connection.

name: Period comparison
purpose: Compare spatial change on the same geographic base.
inputs: Two dates, one projection, and sourced extent data for each period
examples: Territory, administrative boundaries, control, and cultural reach
motion: Keep the scale and viewport fixed. Distinguish uncertain boundaries.

text_slots.t: Keep the scale. Compare the change.
text_slots.note: One map. One scale. Two views.

name: Detail and context
purpose: Bring an overlooked condition into the explanation.
inputs: One source, a close detail, a wider view, and a changed interpretation
examples: The context of a sentence; a face in its surroundings; a detail in an artifact
motion: Start close, then widen the frame while keeping the original subject visible.
